W e describe the case of a 45 year-old female patient, who
over 5 years suffered from painful cramps in the lower and
upper limbs, she had difﬁculty in walking, showed hyperre-
ﬂexia, and an electromyogram showed continuous muscular
activity; she was diagnosed with SPS at the neurology
department and was referred to our urology service for a
urodynamic study because the patient showed difﬁculty in
passing urine, there was a delay in the initiation of micturi-
tion, a weak urinary stream and the sensation of incomplete
emptying after micturition. The patient underwent the afore-
mentioned urodynamic study, which included the following
remarkable alterations:
• Flowmetry: Broken and low micturition ﬂow (Qmax,
6 mL/s) and signiﬁcant post-urinary residues (Fig. 1.1).
• Bladder-ﬁlling cystomanometry: Bladder capacity was
somewhat diminished and showed normal bladder
accommodation and absence of detrusor waves.
• Bladder-emptying cystomanometry through surface
electromyography: Signiﬁcant delay in the initiation of
micturition, low and broken urine ﬂow, and a signiﬁcant
increase of detrusor pressure. Apart from these ﬁndings,
an increased activity of the striated sphincter was also
observed , which reached up to 250 micro-volts
(Fig. 1.2).
Therefore, this condition comprises a detrusor-sphincter
dyssynergia caused by an increment in the activity of the
striated sphincter muscle. The patient was treated with
muscle relaxants, but she left the treatment feeling drowsy,
so she was treated with corticosteroids and she had the same
urinary symptoms.
W e consequently believe that the present urodynamic
study is a useful trial that illustrates the precise urinary
alterations found in patients afﬂicted with SPS, and shows

that it is possible to treat this condition with muscle-
relaxants.
